summary.headline: Indian fast bowler Mohammed Shami retires from Test cricket
summary.summary: Indian fast bowler Mohammed Shami announced his retirement from Test cricket after securing two hundred twenty-nine wickets across sixty-four matches during his career. The thirty-six-year-old athlete, who debuted against the West Indies at Eden Gardens in two thousand thirteen, missed selection for the New Zealand tour due to injury concerns. Shami will continue competing in white-ball formats for the national team.

summary.headline: Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad arrests Maoist in Thane district
summary.summary: The Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad apprehended a 45-year-old Maoist carrying a bounty of 10 lakh rupees from Thakurli in Thane district. The suspect, identified as Sanjay Sarju Yadav alias Godaram Yadav, served as a zonal committee member of a banned organization and had been hiding in the area for ten days. Following the joint intelligence operation with Jharkhand Police, authorities transferred custody of the suspect to Jharkhand law enforcement officers for formal arrest.

summary.headline: Tamil Nadu restructures crop loan waiver scheme and extends deadline
summary.summary: The Tamil Nadu government restructured its crop loan waiver scheme, granting a flat seventy-five thousand rupee waiver to farmers with loans exceeding that amount from cooperative institutions, while retaining full waivers for loans up to seventy-five thousand rupees. Administered by the Cooperation, Food and Consumer Protection Department, the revised initiative extends eligibility to loans obtained up to March 31, 2026, increasing total estimated expenditure to over nine billion rupees.

summary.headline: John Bolton says JD Vance is distancing himself from Donald Trump
summary.summary: Former United States national security adviser John Bolton stated that Vice President JD Vance is attempting to distance himself from President Donald Trump by blaming the Iran war for Republican midterm losses. Bolton described Vance's strategy as politically risky and argued that voter discontent was primarily driven by persistently high prices, inflation, and unfulfilled economic promises. Bolton also warned that ongoing domestic political turmoil in Washington could sideline vital foreign policy priorities, including defense cooperation with India.

summary.headline: Paraguay Senate removes President Santiago Pena from office
summary.summary: Paraguay's Senate voted to remove President Santiago Pena from office and placed him under house arrest following impeachment proceedings initiated against him for misconduct. Vice-President Pedro Alliana was subsequently sworn in as interim President on November 7. Both politicians belong to the Colorado Party, which has remained the dominant political force in Paraguay since the 1940s.

summary.headline: Trump replaces chief of staff Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller
summary.summary: Donald Trump has appointed his longtime adviser and political operative Stephen Miller as White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles following the Republican Party midterm election defeats. Miller is known for his hardline immigration policies and aggressive rhetoric, drawing sharp condemnation from Democrats and some Republicans. His elevation to the influential post signals a potential political battle with Congress rather than an olive branch, raising questions about future legislative negotiations and oversight.

summary.headline: Aviation industry faces disruption from a spate of bomb threats
summary.summary: The global aviation sector is confronting significant operational challenges after experiencing at least thirty-two bomb threats targeting a dozen carriers over four days. Although all incidents were confirmed hoaxes communicated via phone calls and emails, airlines were forced to implement emergency protocols, resulting in diverted flights and military escorts. Experts note the coordinated nature of the threats mirrors hybrid warfare tactics, with perpetrators remaining difficult to trace.

summary.headline: Sudan child malnutrition crisis deepens amid civil war and drought
summary.summary: Severe acute malnutrition is threatening hundreds of thousands of young children across Sudan due to ongoing civil war, displacement, and drought. Medical personnel at facilities like Port Sudan Teaching Hospital report extreme overcrowding and financial strains. According to the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification, hundreds of thousands of children under five are expected to suffer from severe acute malnutrition in 2026, while conflict zones like Darfur and Blue Nile State face worsening humanitarian conditions and inadequate aid.

The court emphasized that enforcement powers are derivative under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act and must strictly follow established legal checks and balances.

Police rescued an eleven-year-old boy and recovered one body while searching multiple disposal sites across Karnataka based on the accused statements regarding family disputes.

summary.headline: Telangana Women's Commission questions inaction over illegal oocyte racket
summary.summary: The Telangana Women's Commission has questioned authorities regarding the lack of legal action against five fertility centres allegedly involved in an illegal egg collection racket in Hyderabad. Forty-three vulnerable women were rescued after being offered between twenty thousand and thirty thousand rupees per cycle, while operators made about three lakh rupees per cycle. Commission Chairperson Nerella Sharada identified the implicated institutions as Indira IVF Centre, Narmada Fertility Centre, Oasis Fertility Centre, Sadguru ART Centre, and Padmaja Fertility Centre, and demanded immediate inquiries and strict legal measures.

summary.summary: The Karnataka Cabinet approved the Sannati Development Authority Bill, 2026, to transform the ancient Buddhist site in Kalaburagi district into an international cultural and tourism destination. Announced by Home Minister Priyank Kharge, the statutory framework aims to conserve Sannati and the neighbouring Kanaganahalli archaeological site, where excavations previously uncovered the Great Stupa of the Netherworlds and inscriptions bearing the name of Emperor Ashoka. The proposed authority will oversee development plans, land acquisition, and regulated construction to address years of site neglect.

summary.headline: Airstrikes in al-Shariya village near Sanaa kill twenty-two people
summary.summary: Attacks hit several homes in al-Shariya village near the Yemeni capital of Sanaa on November 7, 2026, resulting in twenty-two deaths and thirty injuries, mostly among women and children, according to Anees Alasbahi, a spokesman for the Houthi-run Health Ministry. Alasbahi attributed the assault to Saudi Arabia, though the claim remained unverified and the Saudi Information Ministry did not immediately respond. The incident follows a November 6 market strike in southern Yemen that killed at least thirty people amid escalating conflict between the Iranian-backed Houthis and Saudi-backed forces.

summary.headline: Lucknow-bound IndiGo flight returns to Bengaluru following handwritten hijack threat note

Authorities subsequently declared the threat a hoax and launched an investigation to identify who left the note onboard.

card.summary: Justice K. Lakshman of the Telangana High Court awarded a six-month jail term and a 2,000 rupee fine to Ranga Reddy district Collector C. Narayana Reddy for wilful disobedience of a court order. The case originated from a petition filed by P. Shivaleela and P. Venkateshwarlu regarding property documents. The sentence was suspended for four weeks to allow an appeal.

summary.headline: Karnataka High Court issues new guidelines to BMRCL on property access
summary.summary: Justice Suraj Govindaraj of the Karnataka High Court ordered the Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited to assess land acquisition impacts during the planning stage. The court partially allowed a petition from M/s Ellis Fashion Exports Private Limited, imposing ten lakh rupees in costs, and declared specific provisions of the BMRCL Way Leave Policy unconstitutional.

summary.headline: Bengaluru hospitals treat numerous firecracker eye injuries during Deepavali festival
summary.summary: Multiple Bengaluru medical facilities, including Minto Ophthalmic Hospital and Sankara Eye Hospital, reported numerous firecracker-related eye injuries through November 9 during the Deepavali celebrations. Victims included infants and bystanders who sustained severe trauma, burns, and potential vision loss. Doctors emphasised the critical need for adult supervision and protective eyewear during future festive celebrations.

summary.headline: Akhilesh Yadav faces political backlash over proposed Ayodhya temple visit
summary.summary: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav announced plans to visit the Ram Temple in Ayodhya on December 12, drawing criticism from the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party. Political analysts view the upcoming visit as an effort to expand voter outreach beyond traditional bases and blunt opposition rhetoric, while Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath demanded an apology for past actions.

summary.headline: Man arrested in Chhattisgarh for killing four-year-old to sell organs
summary.summary: Basudev Korwa was arrested in Jashpur for allegedly murdering his four-year-old relative to sell his organs after watching an online video. According to Jashpur Senior Superintendent of Police Lal Umed Singh, the agricultural labourer used an artificial intelligence assistant in a chatting app to find methods for making money quickly. Villagers discovered the victim's body after the boy's father filed a missing person complaint.

The measure follows recent government price capping of fine rice varieties and enforcement checks revealing violations.

Iran has not yet responded to these allegations.

summary.headline: Los Angeles elects democratic socialist Nithya Raman as mayor
summary.summary: Los Angeles City Council member Nithya Raman defeated incumbent Karen Bass to win the mayoral race, capturing nearly 53 percent of the vote. Raman, who identifies as a democratic socialist, will take office in December. Her victory highlights the growing political influence of democratic socialists across the United States, as candidates increasingly focus on affordability, cost-of-living issues, and municipal governance to attract working-class voters.

summary.headline: Global carbon emissions drop slightly due to war in Iran

summary.headline: Oxford museum returns ancestral Naga human remains to India
summary.summary: The University of Oxford returned the remains of 39 individuals from the Naga community, acquired during British colonial rule, to an Indian delegation at the Pitt Rivers Museum. Tribal leaders from Nagaland attended the handover ceremony on Monday and plan to bury the remains under a joint memorial. The items were collected between 1910 and 1940 and removed from public display in 2020.

summary.headline: Malaysian court clears former prime minister Najib Razak for house arrest
summary.summary: A Kuala Lumpur high court ruled that former Prime Minister Najib Razak will serve the remainder of his reduced six-year sentence under house arrest following a conditional pardon. Judge Aslam Zainuddin delivered the decision on Tuesday after an earlier delay by the attorney general over legal interpretations. Najib remains convicted in connection with the 1Malaysia Development Berhad scandal and faces additional prison terms.

card.summary: A United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon patrol faced about a dozen rounds of gunfire near Wadi Jilu in the Tyre district on Tuesday, according to the peacekeeping mission. The unit returned fire and reported no casualties before calling for an investigation. The incident highlights ongoing security concerns as G7 foreign ministers debate the future of the force ahead of its mandate expiration in December 2026.
card.description: UNIFIL said on Tuesday that 'about a dozen rounds' were fired at one of its patrols, without identifying the assailants.

summary.headline: Gallup poll shows death penalty support falls below fifty percent
summary.summary: A Gallup survey released on Tuesday revealed that support for capital punishment in the United States dropped to 49 percent, marking the first time the practice lost majority support since 1971. The findings reflect decades of declining approval across age groups and political parties amid concerns regarding fairness and high costs. Twenty-seven states currently retain the death penalty despite shifting public sentiment.

summary.headline: IBM's largest division ends most United States foreign worker sponsorships
summary.summary: United States technology firm IBM confirmed on Tuesday that its consultancy division will discontinue sponsoring foreign worker visas and green cards for most positions. A company spokesperson told Reuters that reliance on high-skilled visa programmes had decreased alongside shifting client needs. The announcement follows increased pressure from the administration of President Donald Trump regarding the employment of foreign technology workers.

summary.headline: Escitalopram outperforms other antidepressants in preventing patient relapse during analysis
summary.summary: An analysis published in The Lancet Psychiatry examined nearly 10,000 patients and found that the antidepressant escitalopram was most effective at preventing relapse over a period of up to a year. Agomelatine and duloxetine ranked next, while fluoxetine ranked just below. Experts emphasized that the differences are modest and patients should consult doctors regarding individual factors before changing any treatments.

The victim's father alleged that online harassment and extortion by Samuel drove his son to take his own life after Meta disabled Instagram accounts for lacking Securities and Exchange Board of India registration. Samuel denied cyberbullying allegations, stating he acted to protect consumers.
card.description: V Harish, who ran the hugely popular Instagram account "Finance with Harish", was found dead on Tuesday.

summary.headline: Hundreds of Italian schools receive bomb threats in suspected cyber-attack
summary.summary: Approximately 300 schools across Italy received bomb threats on Wednesday, prompting precautionary evacuations before authorities lifted the alarms. Education Minister Giuseppe Valditara stated that the emails were likely part of a broader cyber-attack strategy intended to cause alarm across Europe, mirroring recent hoaxes targeting airports. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni convened top ministers and intelligence chiefs, noting no evidence of concrete danger.

summary.headline: Kenya discharges final Ebola patient and starts countdown to virus-free status
summary.summary: Kenya has discharged its seventh and final Ebola patient, marking a key milestone in its response to an outbreak that began in October following an importation from the Democratic Republic of Congo. Health Minister Aden Duale announced that all tracked contacts have completed monitoring, leaving the nation to begin a 42-day countdown toward an official virus-free declaration under World Health Organization guidelines.

summary.headline: Cairo court adjourns retrial of journalist Lina Attalah amid UN criticism

The United Nations has criticized the case, warning of widening assaults on press freedom by Egyptian authorities against independent newsrooms.

card.summary: Manchester United appointed Mauricio Pochettino as their new manager on November 13, 2026, following the dismissal of Michael Carrick. The 54-year-old Argentine coach signed a two-and-a-half-year deal after concluding his duties with the United States men's national team. Pochettino faces the challenge of reviving the struggling Premier League club, which currently sits in the relegation zone after winning only one of its first ten matches.
card.description: The 54-year-old is understood to have signed a two-and-a-half-year deal at Old Trafford, taking him through to the end of the 2028/29 season

summary.headline: Anthropic tests consumer AI agent Duet for professionals and small business owners
summary.summary: Anthropic has released a research preview of Claude Duet, a consumer artificial intelligence agent designed to assist professionals and small business owners in the United States who subscribe to Pro, Max, and Ultra tiers. Operating through a dedicated application on the iPhone Duo, the tool integrates work emails, calendars, Google Documents, and Slack to manage daily schedules and suggest tasks.

card.headline: Anthropic tests consumer AI agent Duet for professionals and small business owners
card.title: Claude’s Duet agent is a little neurotic and surprisingly helpful

summary.headline: Nitin Gadkari says world-class roads are vital for India's economic growth
summary.summary: Union Minister Nitin Gadkari stated that advanced road infrastructure is essential for national economic progress and Andhra Pradesh development during the 31st CII Partnership Summit on November 13, 2026. Highlighting projects like the Surat–Chennai Expressway and Amaravati Outer Ring Road, he noted that the National Highway network in the State expanded significantly between 2014 and 2026, while State Minister B.C. Janardhan Reddy emphasized investment opportunities.

summary.headline: Telangana Women's Commission probes ART centres over illegal oocyte racket
summary.summary: The Telangana State Women's Commission initiated an inquiry into an alleged illegal egg donation racket on November 13, 2026, issuing notices to eight Assisted Reproductive Technology centres. Chairperson Nerella Sharada expressed dissatisfaction with institutional representation and questioned claims that ninety percent of donors were voluntary and unremunerated, prompting discussions on strengthening regulatory oversight with health officials.

summary.headline: SP and Congress say AIMIM-ASP alliance will not impact INDIA bloc
summary.summary: Leaders from the Samajwadi Party and Congress stated on November 13, 2026, that the newly formed Samajik Parivartan Morcha alliance between AIMIM and the Azad Samaj Party will not affect INDIA bloc prospects in upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. While acknowledging potential minor vote shifts, representatives argued that voters recognize the BJP alternative, following the alliance announcement by Asaduddin Owaisi and Chandrashekhar Azad.

summary.headline: Kerala High Court calls lack of KIIFB CAG audit concerning
summary.summary: The Kerala High Court observed that the previous State government's failure to subject KIIFB accounts to a Comptroller and Auditor General audit was concerning, noting preliminary discrepancies. The court disposed of a public interest litigation after noting the current government's decision to comprehensively audit the board, which held outstanding loan liabilities amounting to over twenty thousand crore rupees by March 31, 2024.

summary.headline: Pakistan calls for immediate cessation of Houthi attacks
summary.summary: Pakistan demanded an immediate and unconditional halt to Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia during a United Nations Security Council session on Thursday, November 12, 2026. Pakistan's Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Syed Haider Shah, expressed full solidarity with Saudi Arabia's security, as the council unanimously adopted a resolution renewing targeted sanctions for another year.

Usha, the collaborative platform showcases artificial intelligence, analytics, and venue management tools designed to help sports organisations improve performance and fan engagement.

summary.headline: Truck and bus collision in Assam leaves twenty-four dead
summary.summary: At least twenty-four people were killed and eleven others injured following a head-on collision between a container truck and a bus in India's northeastern state of Assam on Friday. Police confirmed the tragedy occurred on a highway in the Golaghat district near Kaziranga National Park, prompting Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma to express deep distress over the heavy loss of life.

summary.headline: European leaders debate representation in Russia-Ukraine peace talks
summary.summary: Leaders of the twenty-seven European Union member states met at a summit in Dublin, Ireland, on Friday to discuss how the continent should be represented in ongoing negotiations between Washington, Kyiv, and Moscow. While figures like European Union foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas and European Council President Antonio Costa are contenders, European officials remain divided on whether to send a single envoy or a team.

summary.headline: Democrats hold leverage to strip US-Israel military integration from Pentagon bill
summary.summary: Advocates state that Democratic lawmakers possess the congressional leverage necessary to remove a controversial measure from the National Defense Authorization Act before a December 11 funding deadline. Section 219 of the Senate bill establishes the United States-Israel Defense Technology Cooperation Initiative. Critics warn this bypasses congressional oversight, while progressive groups urge party leaders to block the legislation until the integration provision is completely eliminated.

summary.summary: American Grandmaster Abhimanyu Mishra drew both of his round-three matches against world number one Magnus Carlsen during the Total Chess World Championship Tour pilot on Thursday, November 13, 2026. summary.headline: Armed men kill 37 civilians in western Niger ambush
summary.summary: Armed men killed at least 37 civilians in an ambush in western Niger on November 12, 2026, according to local sources. The attack targeted villagers travelling to a market in Tera within the Tillaberi region. The dead included members of a local self defence group and residents. Conflict monitors note the region is a jihadist violence epicentre.

summary.headline: Syria rescinds entry restrictions for United States travellers
summary.summary: Syria reversed a temporary interior ministry directive requiring United States citizens to obtain prior visa authorisation on November 13, 2026, following online complaints. Ports and borders authority official Mazen Allouch confirmed entry procedures returned to previous rules allowing Americans to obtain visas at Damascus airport or border crossings. Tourism has risen following the 2024 government transition.

summary.summary: At least 24 people died and 11 others were injured after a bus collided with a truck in Assam, north-east India, near Kaziranga National Park. The injured were admitted to Jorhat Medical College and Hospital.

summary.headline: Sixth victim found following Washington condo dispute shooting

summary.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent advised the Federal Reserve on Friday against increasing interest rates due to an energy supply shock from the conflict with Iran. summary.headline: Tamil Nadu government imposes stock limits on paddy, rice and pulses
summary.summary: The Tamil Nadu government imposed stock limits on paddy, rice, tur dal, and pulses across the State to prevent hoarding and curb food inflation, according to orders issued on November 14, 2026. Wholesalers and retailers must clear excess stocks by November 16 under the new regulations, which remain in force until early 2027 to ensure fair pricing and equitable distribution.

summary.headline: COP31 talks face sluggish climate finance responses amid Western security pressures
summary.summary: Urgent demands for climate finance from vulnerable developing nations met a slow response at the COP31 summit in Antalya as Western governments prioritized national security and domestic living costs. Host country Turkiye and Australia focused on implementing existing pledges rather than setting new targets. While multilateral development banks reported record lending in 2025, analysts noted significant funding gaps driven by geopolitical tensions, constrained fiscal spaces, and high capital costs.

summary.headline: Ukraine launches massive drone barrage as peace negotiators discuss European security
summary.summary: Ukraine fired nearly 1,200 drones at Russian targets overnight in one of its largest aerial attacks, according to Russia’s Defence Ministry, resulting in seven deaths and seventeen injuries across three regions. Simultaneously, United States envoys held discussions in Abu Dhabi and Moscow regarding potential peace talks, agreeing to include wider post-Cold War European security arrangements. European Union leaders, including diplomatic chief Kaja Kallas, cautioned against Russian traps and insisted on prioritizing an immediate ceasefire.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy stated that airspace reopened after four hours of disruption, which cancelled thousands of flights, stranded passengers, and prompted calls for significant air traffic control system upgrades.
card.description: The FAA says nationwide ground stop disrupting thousands of US flights was caused by a telecommunications outage.

summary.headline: Measles-associated deaths reach ten in the United States after two new fatalities
summary.summary: Pennsylvania and Wisconsin announced new measles-associated fatalities, bringing the United States total to ten deaths this year alongside more than 5,400 confirmed cases. A federal dispute emerged between state officials and United States Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. regarding how fatalities are classified. Infectious disease experts warn the ongoing outbreak threatens the nation's measles elimination status achieved in 2000.

summary.headline: SpaceX launches 15th Starship flight aiming for first round trip
summary.summary: SpaceX launched its 15th uncrewed Starship spacecraft from South Texas on November 13, 2026, aiming to achieve the first successful orbital round trip and tower catch. While the upper stage reached orbit to deploy Starlink satellites, the Super Heavy booster deviated from its flight path and exploded over the Gulf of Mexico, marking a setback for Elon Musk's reusable rocket development program funded partly by NASA.

summary.headline: Indian chef Ranji Smile introduced curry to America
summary.summary: Ranji Smile, an enigmatic Indian chef, arrived in New York in 1899 and opened the first Indian restaurant in the United States, Sherry's Restaurant, before launching his own establishment named Omar Khayyam in 1901. Despite initial fame and theatrical presentations, the restaurant closed within a year, and Smile subsequently faced legal troubles, federal investigations regarding staff trafficking, and eventual obscurity by the 1920s.

summary.headline: US air traffic control system outage causes longest ground stop since 9/11
summary.summary: The United States Federal Aviation Administration lifted a nationwide ground stop that lasted more than four hours on Friday due to a communication issue affecting air traffic control centres. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy explained that analogue telecom switches and routers became overloaded with data, causing thousands of flight delays and cancellations in the longest nationwide stoppage since September 11, 2001.

summary.headline: Kurumba community in Kerala struggles to preserve unwritten language

Because outsiders do not speak this language, community members must learn Malayalam and other regional languages for external communication.

summary.summary: The Kerala High Court stated that police possess full authority to enforce measures addressing drug and substance abuse across the state. summary.headline: Central Bureau of Investigation conducts searches across six states in Mahadev betting app case
summary.summary: The Central Bureau of Investigation executed searches at 33 locations across six states on November 14, 2026, recovering digital devices and documents related to the Mahadev online betting platform. Operations spanned Delhi, Mumbai, Nagpur, Amritsar, Bhopal, and Raipur based on disclosures from extradited promoter Sourabh Chandrakar. Officials stated that panel operators utilized mule bank accounts and hawala channels to transfer illegal profits abroad.

summary.headline: Oral GLP-1 medications offer new treatment options for diabetes and obesity
summary.summary: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist therapies are shifting from weekly injections to once-daily pills, potentially increasing global access to diabetes and obesity treatments. Oral options eliminate the need for cold-chain refrigeration, making distribution easier in emerging economies where high diabetes rates persist. Pakistan leads global prevalence at 31.4 percent, while medical experts highlight that these medications also improve cardiac, renal, and liver conditions.

summary.headline: Kerala High Court rules Tantri holds no ownership over deity assets
summary.summary: The Kerala High Court determined that a temple Tantri possesses authority solely over religious rituals rather than legal ownership of deity assets. A division bench comprising Justices K.V. Jayakumar and Raja Vijayaraghavan V. dismissed a petition challenging a 2012 circular from the Travancore Devaswom Board, upholding statutory management frameworks for temple properties.

summary.headline: Surging onion prices create severe financial distress for consumers in Kochi
summary.summary: Retail markets in Kochi experienced a significant spike in onion prices, with shallots reaching up to ₹180 per kilogram due to low yields and supply shortages from Tamil Nadu. summary.headline: NASA space probe Voyager 1 approaches milestone of one light-day distance
summary.summary: NASA has announced that the Voyager 1 space probe will soon reach a distance of one light-day from Earth, having travelled at least 16 billion miles since its 1977 launch. Currently operating in interstellar space at approximately 36,000 miles per hour, the plutonium-powered craft continues to transmit daily scientific data alongside its twin, Voyager 2. Project manager Suzanne Dodd described the mission as a national treasure while noting ongoing communication efforts by a skeleton engineering team.

The Health Ministry reported that the proportion of out-of-pocket spending by households fell from 64.2% to 42.7% over the decade. The data highlights expanded public financing, increased primary healthcare spending, and growth in government and private health insurance schemes across the country.
card.description: The share of healthcare costs borne by households fell from 64.2% to 42.7% over a decade, while social security spending on health rose from 6% to 11%

card.summary: India's Ministry of Defence announced on 4 November that soldiers finishing four-year terms under the Agnipath programme can serve two additional years at higher pay. Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani stated the decision followed internal reviews. More than 18,300 recruits will complete their initial tenure by the end of 2026, amid ongoing debates regarding training duration and military effectiveness.
card.description: India has softened its recruitment scheme, giving young soldiers a longer military stint and another shot at permanent service.

summary.headline: Notorious Mexican drug lord Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo dies in hospital at age 80
summary.summary: Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo, founder of the Guadalajara Cartel and a pioneer of international drug smuggling alliances, died in a Guadalajara hospital at age 80. Known as The Godfather, he orchestrated partnerships with Colombian cartels during the 1980s cocaine boom. He had remained in state custody since his arrest in 1989 following the murder of Drug Enforcement Administration agent Enrique Camarena.

summary.headline: Steering failure preceded New Orleans cruise ship collision

summary.headline: Astronomers discover unusual pair of distant quasars in the early universe
summary.summary: Astronomers have identified a strange pair of quasars located just 18,100 light-years apart when the universe was only 900 million years old. summary.headline: New book examines Jawaharlal Nehru through intelligence chief Bhola Nath Mullik
summary.summary: A recently published analysis explores the professional relationship between India's inaugural Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and his longtime intelligence leader, Bhola Nath Mullik. The publication highlights a rarely examined operational dimension of the administration.

card.summary: Nineteen-year-old Russian tennis player Mirra Andreeva defeated Ukraine's Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 on November 15, 2026, to win the WTA Finals without dropping a set at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden. Svitolina collected 1.5 million dollars after finishing as the runner-up in the eight-day tournament, according to the match report.

summary.headline: US hyperscale data centers consume massive amounts of electricity
summary.summary: A study published in Nature Sustainability reveals that four hundred three United States hyperscale data centers consumed approximately eighty-two terawatt-hours of electricity from May 2024 to April 2025. Researchers Gianluca Guidi and his team used satellite imagery to estimate power consumption, noting that fifty-four percent of the energy likely came from gas and coal, generating millions of metric tons of carbon dioxide.

summary.headline: Houthi rebel offensive on Yemen coast threatens global economic stability

summary.headline: Government raises export duties on diesel and aviation turbine fuel

Diesel exports face a levy of 14 rupees per litre, and aviation turbine fuel reaches 12.5 rupees per litre.

summary.headline: Six Liangmai Naga civilians laid to rest in Manipur

summary.headline: Eelam Tamil poet and academic Rudhramoorthy Cheran dies at 68
summary.summary: Rudhramoorthy Cheran, an Eelam Tamil poet, essayist, and professor of sociology and criminology at the University of Windsor, passed away in Canada at the age of 68. Hailing from Jaffna, he emerged as a leading voice of wartime literature and diasporic experiences, chronicling decades of Tamil life. His celebrated works have been translated into multiple languages, and he is survived by his wife and two children.

The India Meteorological Department reported that Ichchapuram mandal received 153.25 millimetres. Gale winds reached 100 kilometres per hour near the center as the landfall process began near Gopalpur.
card.description: The major rainfall activity has been concentrated in the district of Srikakulam alone, while a few stations in Vizianagaram, Anakapalli, Kakinada, Visakhapatnam, have recorded light showers

summary.headline: Yadadri Thermal Power Station ash pollutes Telangana stream
summary.summary: Residents of Veerlapalem village in Telangana's Nalgonda district raised concerns over ash slurry pollution in the Thungapahad stream caused by the Yadadri Thermal Power Station. Farmer V. Nageshwar Rao filed a complaint with the Telangana Pollution Control Board in May 2026, prompting a show-cause notice issued to the Telangana Power Generation Corporation Limited the following month.

summary.headline: Madhya Pradesh scraps two-child policy for government employees
summary.summary: The Madhya Pradesh Cabinet approved scrapping the twenty-five-year-old two-child restriction policy for government employees and job applicants, citing declining fertility rates. Chief Minister Mohan Yadav announced the decision on November 18, 2026, at a meeting in Mandsaur district. Officials stated the rule caused difficulties and that ongoing disciplinary proceedings regarding child counts will terminate immediately, aligning with broader demographic debates on falling birth rates.

summary.headline: Justice Nagarathna says high offices do not ensure equality
summary.summary: Supreme Court Justice B.V. Nagarathna stated that women holding high public office does not prove that societal equality has been achieved. Delivering the Cornelia Sorabji Memorial Lecture at the University of Oxford on November 18, 2026, she emphasized that substantive equality requires addressing intersecting structural disadvantages like caste, class, and unpaid domestic labor. She noted that formal legislation alone cannot guarantee safety, education, or inheritance rights for all women.

The Election Commission of India maintained it was removing ineligible voters, while the Ministry of External Affairs dismissed the USCIRF criticism as biased.

summary.headline: Indian food inflation reaches 8.9% with significant price increases across essential commodities.
summary.summary: Food inflation across India reached 8.9% last month, marking the highest rate recorded in twenty-two months according to official data. Retail prices for essential commodities surged between January and October, led by onions increasing by more than 100% since March. Garlic prices rose by 22% and rice increased by 11%, contributing to a 16% jump in the average cost of a meal.

Meta reported a 45 percent increase in net carbon-equivalent emissions to 11.8 million tonnes in 2025. This shift follows broader corporate environmental retreats under United States President Donald Trump.

summary.headline: Andhra Pradesh faces severe coastal erosion along thirty-one percent of shorelines
summary.summary: Satellite mapping by the National Centre for Coastal Research under the Union Ministry of Earth Sciences revealed that nearly thirty-one percent of Andhra Pradesh's coastline is eroding. Published in February 2024, the Shoreline Change Atlas indicated severe losses concentrated in delta districts like Kakinada and West Godavari, while local experts noted direct wave impacts along Visakhapatnam roads.

summary.headline: Chinese Communist Party publishes revised regulations for local committees
summary.summary: The Chinese Communist Party published revised regulations on Monday detailing governance rules for local committees across provincial, city, and county levels. The updated text removes references to Marxism-Leninism and Mao Zedong Thought, replacing them with Xi Jinping Thought as the primary guide. It also expands the political remits and oversight powers held by higher-level committees over local staff.

This victory made him the first Italian to claim the title since Alberto Ascari in 1953, watched live across Italy.

summary.headline: Government extends validity of pollution certificates for newer vehicles
summary.summary: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has modified regulations surrounding Pollution Under Control Certificates by connecting mandatory emission testing frequency directly to vehicle age and emission standards. Under the revised norms, specific newer Bharat Stage VI vehicles are granted a certificate validity of up to three years, thereby reducing the regular frequency of required vehicle pollution checks across the country.

Professionals in technology and academia report experiencing increased scrutiny and skepticism in workplaces, compounding long-standing historical prejudices and reinforcing detrimental misconceptions regarding competence, leadership, and trustworthiness across the United States.
card.description: Asian American women working in tech, civil rights advocacy and academia have felt a sense of dread that this ordeal will diminish how their peers are viewed and treated in their workplaces. It’s a reminder that no accomplishments will completely dispel centuries-old stereotypes

summary.headline: Prime Minister Modi criticizes corporate India over domestic manufacturing progress

summary.headline: Russian missile strikes target Kyiv bridges and kill six people
summary.summary: Russia launched nearly one hundred missiles and four hundred drones targeting Ukrainian infrastructure, hitting three Dnipro River bridges in Kyiv and killing six individuals. Additional strikes in Lviv claimed two lives at a railway station, while Polish forces investigated a projectile landing near the border. Officials reported widespread injuries, power disruptions, and ongoing air raid sirens across nine regions.

summary.headline: Nigerian President Bola Tinubu proposes decriminalising attempted suicide
summary.summary: Nigerian President Bola Tinubu has asked parliament to replace criminal penalties for attempted suicide with medical treatment, rehabilitation, and support services. The proposal follows years of advocacy from mental health professionals who argued that prosecuting survivors discourages individuals from seeking help, while Senate President Godswill Akpabio referred the amendment bill to a senate committee for further consideration.

summary.headline: El Salvador president launches controversial third term re-election campaign

summary.headline: Muslim population projected to surpass Christians globally by 2035
summary.summary: Muslims are projected to outnumber Christians globally by 2035, driven by higher fertility rates according to Pew Research Center data. Between 2020 and 2070, the global Muslim population is expected to rise by 80 percent to 3.64 billion. Pakistan is projected to overtake Indonesia with the largest Muslim population, while India and Nigeria will also see significant growth.

card.headline: Spacecraft BepiColombo approaches final orbit around Mercury after eight-year journey
card.title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage
card.summary: The BepiColombo spacecraft, a joint mission by the European Space Agency and the Japanese Space Agency launched in 2018 from French Guiana, is preparing to enter Mercury's orbit after travelling nearly six billion miles. The mission aims to study the planet's extreme temperatures, ice in craters, and mysterious hollows. Once arrived, the two onboard spacecraft will separate to examine the harsh and little-explored inner Solar System planet closely.
card.description: The mission is set to give us our best ever view of Mercury - the closest planet to the Sun.

card.summary: Iranian forces intercepted and shot down two United States drones over the Strait of Hormuz, according to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. The incident occurred on Saturday amid ongoing military tensions and stalled diplomatic efforts to end the conflict. Meanwhile, the United States Treasury imposed new sanctions on four Iranian individuals accused of acting as oil trustees to evade maritime blockades.
card.description: Iran reiterates conditions for Hormuz reopening as US slaps sanctions on four Iranians it says acted as 'oil trustees'.

summary.headline: French court finds three police officers guilty of racially motivated assault
summary.summary: A Paris criminal court convicted three police officers of intentional racist violence and falsifying reports during the 2020 assault of music producer Michel Zecler. The defendants received five-year prison sentences with varying suspended portions and permanent bans from the force. The incident drew renewed scrutiny regarding systemic brutality and discrimination within French law enforcement agencies.

card.title: French police officers guilty of Michel Zecler assault: What happens now?

card.description: Officers dealt more than 30 blows to the Black music producer in what the court ruled was a racially motivated crime.

summary.headline: Harry Kane to miss few months after tearing ankle ligament
summary.summary: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane will sidelined for several months following a syndesmosis ligament tear in his left ankle. The injury occurred during a 1-1 draw against Cologne when defender Joel Schmied collided with him. The outcome leaves the Bundesliga leaders without their key forward as they maintain their position at the top of the table.

summary.headline: Illicit alcohol kills eleven people and poisons one hundred eighty in Manipur state
summary.summary: At least eleven people died and more than one hundred eighty individuals were hospitalized after consuming toxic illicit alcohol in northeast India's Manipur state. Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh confirmed the fatalities and hospitalizations in a statement issued on Friday. Authorities advised residents in Sugnu town to seek medical evaluation following the consumption of unregulated liquor.

summary.headline: CCMB researchers identify genes that stimulate nerve regeneration
summary.summary: Scientists at the CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology in Hyderabad have identified two developmental genes, NR2F1 and NR2F6, that restore the ability of damaged nerve cells to regenerate. Published in The EMBO Journal on November 20, 2026, the preclinical study demonstrated that restoring these genes in mice led to severed nerve fibres regrowing across spinal cords and improved mobility, offering a potential framework for treating paralysis.

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy launched the scheme in Siddipet. A month-long rural and urban enrolment drive requires Aadhaar and ration cards for applicants aged eighteen to fifty-nine years.

Representatives from the Indian Army and Ministry of Defence witnessed the November demonstration. Developed over eighteen months, the system features automated launchers mounted on high-mobility armoured vehicles to enhance combat capabilities.

summary.headline: Congress launches Uttar Pradesh OBC outreach campaign demanding caste census

According to AICC OBC Department National Chairman Anil Jaihind, the party advocates for proportional representation and intends to challenge the twenty-seven percent reservation cap once enumeration data is released. He also noted that Rahul Gandhi is expected to address upcoming December events.

summary.summary: The ruling Bharatiya Janata Party faced significant electoral setbacks in rural Rajasthan panchayat polls despite previous success in urban local body elections. Seventeen state ministers and three Union ministers failed to defend their local political strongholds. The opposition Congress secured major gains by winning hundreds of zila parishad and panchayat samiti seats, highlighting stark contrasts between urban and rural voter sentiment across the state.

card.title: Sudan’s elderly face hardship and heartbreak in a life of displacement

Officials emphasize the urgent need for specialized humanitarian assistance and social protection services for vulnerable older populations.

State Health Minister Satya Kumar Yadav attributed the success to enhanced monitoring via the Suraksha portal and targeted community initiatives.

summary.headline: History of world chess championships and legendary players examined
summary.summary: Emanuel Lasker held the record as the longest-reigning world chess champion for twenty-seven years, beginning in 1894 when he defeated Wilhelm Steinitz in New York, Philadelphia, and Montreal. According to The Hindu, Lasker was also a mathematician and philosopher. His reign ended in 1921 against Jose Raul Capablanca. Subsequent champions included Alexander Alekhine and Max Euwe before Alekhine died holding the title in 1946.
